name: MemGen: Weaving Generative Latent Memory for Self-Evolving Agents
venue: arXiv:2509.24704 (cs.CL); accepted at ICLR 2026 (per official GitHub README)
authors_affiliation: Guibin Zhang (co-first), Muxin Fu (co-first), Shuicheng Yan; National University of Singapore
code_url: https://github.com/bingreeky/MemGen (also reachable via https://github.com/KANABOON1/MemGen); checkpoints at https://huggingface.co/Kana-s/MemGen
maintained_repo_url: N/A (single-paper code repo, not a maintained leaderboard/paper-list)
task_domain: Multi-domain LLM-agent decision-making and reasoning: web/open-domain QA (TriviaQA, PopQA), embodied action (ALFWorld), math reasoning (AQuA, GSM8K, MATH), scientific reasoning (GPQA), and code generation (KodCode, BigCodeBench).
problem_setting: Agent memory for self-evolving LLM agents. An agent powered by a frozen core LLM (the 'reasoner') interacts with an environment, producing trajectories tau=(s0,a0,...,sT) whose success is scored by a reward R(tau). Given a history of past experiences H={(x_i,tau_i)}, the goal is to jointly leverage memory M and policy pi_theta to maximize expected reward on new tasks. Setting is single-agent; supervision comes from official training splits of the evaluated datasets (task reward / answer correctness). MemGen trains lightweight memory modules (LoRA adapters) on these experiences while keeping the reasoner frozen; both offline training and test-time autoregressive generation are interactive at the token level. Positioned against parametric memory (which alters reasoner weights) and retrieval-based memory (which externalizes experience to a database).
what_is_retrieved: Machine-native latent memory: a fixed-length sequence of K latent token embeddings (M_t in R^{K x d_model}) generated on the fly by a learned 'memory weaver' from the agent's current hidden cognitive state. It is generated/synthesized rather than retrieved from a text store; optionally textual experiences can be retrieved from an external memory system (e.g., MemoryBank, ExpeL) and fused into the weaver's input (Appendix E).
retrieval_grounding: Primarily GROWING/internalized parametric memory: experiences are internalized into the weaver's LoRA parameters (a generative, not database, store). Can be HYBRID: an external retrieval system can supply textual memory that is merged with the hook and fed to the weaver. Default mode does not query a static external corpus.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Neither top-k ranking nor completeness recovery. There is no ranked candidate set; the weaver generates a fixed-length latent memory M_t of K tokens (K in {2,4,8}, ablated 2->32) at each invocation. The 'selection' decision is binary INVOKE/SKIP per sentence boundary, learned to be sparse and strategically placed.
cbr_cycle_coverage: Not framed as CBR. Loosely: Retrieve = generative recall of latent memory (no discrete case retrieval); Reuse = latent tokens woven into reasoning; Revise = N/A (no explicit case adaptation); Retain = experiences internalized into weaver LoRA parameters during training. Flags: [Retrieve(generative), Reuse, no-Revise, Retain(parametric)].
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The paper does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner; it is framed via human cognitive neuroscience analogy (hippocampus/prefrontal cortex, working/procedural/planning memory).
retrieval_unit: Latent token sequence / soft tokens: a fixed-length K-by-d_model matrix of continuous hidden-state embeddings ('machine-native latent memory'), generated per invocation. Not a discrete demo, trajectory, document, or tool.
index_source: Growing/online-induced parametric store: experiential knowledge from offline training trajectories is internalized exclusively into the memory weaver's LoRA parameters (reasoner left frozen). No discrete external index by default; an optional hybrid mode can attach a retrieval database. The latent memory itself is regenerated at inference (test-time) conditioned on the current state.
index_structure_topology: No explicit index structure (the 'store' is the weaver's parameters). Emergent organization: post-hoc t-SNE/K-means analysis shows generated latent memories self-cluster by domain and by functional role (planning / procedural / working memory), i.e., an implicit, unsupervised hierarchical organization rather than an engineered topology.
retriever_type: Generative neural module ('memory weaver'): a LoRA adapter on the frozen reasoner that maps the current hidden-state context H_{t,<j} to a latent memory matrix M_t. This is generation-as-retrieval (no BM25/dense/index lookup in the default setting).
retriever_learning_signal: Learned via downstream task reward. The weaver is trained to maximize expected reward R over past trajectories, with two variants: MemGen-SFT (supervised/SFT-style updates) and MemGen-GRPO (RL with GRPO). The memory trigger is trained separately by reinforcement learning with a reward-adaptive sparsity penalty. Both modules optimized for task effectiveness, not similarity labels.
query_construction: The 'query'/stimulus is the reasoner's current internal cognitive state: the sequence of hidden-state vectors H_{t,<j}=(h_{t,1},...,h_{t,j-1}) accumulated up to the current token j. This same hook is consumed by both the trigger (to decide INVOKE/SKIP) and the weaver (to synthesize M_t). No textual query is formed by default.
query_granularity: Token/sentence-level (fine-grained, within-step). The trigger evaluates at delimiter tokens (commas, periods) during action generation, so memory is invoked at sentence granularity within each reasoning step, far finer than task-level (Expel) or step-level (AgentKB) invocation.
when_to_retrieve: Active / adaptive: a learned memory trigger decides on-demand, at sentence boundaries during token-by-token generation, whether to invoke memory (INVOKE vs SKIP). Frequency self-adapts to task difficulty (more invocations on harder/familiar domains, fewer in unfamiliar ones).
retrieval_trigger_signal: Learned trigger over the reasoner's hidden states. A LoRA-based trigger T_trigger reads H_{t,<j} and outputs an invocation probability p_j=sigma(T_trigger(...)); d_j ~ Bernoulli(p_j) in {INVOKE,SKIP}. Gated to fire only at a predefined delimiter token set D (sentence-granularity activation). Trained by RL with a reward-adaptive penalty using mean activation probability of high-reward trajectories as the reference threshold p-bar.
reranking: None. No candidate set is produced or reranked; memory is generated directly as latent tokens.
retrieved_context_refinement: None in the conventional sense. The latent memory is itself a 'selective reconstruction' synthesized by the weaver (analogized to hippocampal consolidation) rather than a verbatim restatement; no rerank/compress/distill stage over retrieved text. Optional hybrid mode fuses external textual memory into the weaver input before latent synthesis.
index_content_separation: N/A (no separated lightweight index vs heavy content; memory is generated from weaver parameters).
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no external tool index or integration protocol).
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no tool retrieval; no inter-tool dependency modeling).
how_retrieved_used: Latent-token injection. The generated latent memory M_t is prepended to the reasoner's current hidden states H_{t,<j}; the frozen reasoner then resumes autoregressive generation conditioned on this enriched context (a_t ~ pi_theta(.|s_t, z_{t,<j}, M_t)). Memory directly conditions the model's internal computation rather than being appended as prompt text.
planning_integration: Per-step / per-token interleaved within reasoning. Memory is woven into the ongoing generation autoregressively (generate -> monitor -> invoke -> weave -> reintegrate), turning linear decoding into a 'recursive dialogue with memory'. Not plan-then-retrieve or one-shot exemplars; invocation can occur many times within a single action/step.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-sentence / per-token within a rollout: the trigger evaluates at delimiter (sentence-boundary) tokens during each action's token generation, finer than per-CoT-step and far finer than per-answer.
adaptation_mechanism: Latent. Retrieved/generated memory is not adapted as a discrete case; instead the weaver synthesizes a state-conditioned latent representation that is injected into hidden states. Experiential adaptation lives in the weaver's trained LoRA parameters (SFT or GRPO).
retrieved_item_representation: Latent / soft tokens: continuous hidden-state embeddings (K x d_model), machine-native and human-unreadable (forced decoding yields non-natural-language but structurally regular token patterns). Not raw text, trajectory, program, or structured note.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Distilled latent strategy/insight at sub-symbolic level. Post-hoc analysis maps clusters to abstract functional roles (planning memory for high-level strategy, procedural memory for tool-use/formatting operations, working memory for context retention) rather than raw trajectories or single demonstrations.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Learned selective invocation as the main guard: the RL-trained trigger with reward-adaptive sparsity penalty avoids spurious/unnecessary memory insertions that could disrupt reasoning; sentence-granularity gating aligns injection with semantic boundaries. Ablations show trained-trigger > all-delimiter activation > random insertion, evidencing interference control. The frozen reasoner also preserves base capabilities.
memory_type: Latent (generative latent memory). Self-organizes into an emergent human-like hierarchy of planning, procedural, and working memory; distinct from episodic database, skill-library, workflow, or graph memory.
write_back: True (at training time, parametric). Experiences are internalized into the memory weaver's LoRA parameters during SFT/GRPO training; the reasoner is never modified. There is no discrete episodic database write; 'write-back' is parameter consolidation rather than appending records.
online_growth: Partial / [uncertain]. The retrievable store (weaver parameters) grows during offline/continual training phases, and a continual-learning protocol (sequential AQuA->GPQA->GSM8K->KodCode) demonstrates incremental accumulation. At pure inference the latent memory is regenerated per query but parameters are frozen; the framework supports continual training rather than autonomous test-time database growth.
write_back_trigger: On training over experiences (reward-driven). Weaver/trigger parameters are updated from batches of past trajectories using their rewards (SFT or GRPO). Not per-step episodic appends; not reflective text writes; no human validation. In continual learning, each new task stage triggers a parameter update.
failure_experience_usage: Reward-graded (implicit success+failure). Training uses full reward signals over trajectories (GRPO/REINFORCE-style and SFT), so low-reward (failed) trajectories shape the gradient; the trigger's reward-adaptive penalty uses high-reward trajectories (reward >= batch median) to set the sparsity reference. No explicit separate failure-only corrective-rule store.
memory_evolution_update: Refine/overwrite via gradient updates to weaver and trigger LoRA parameters (parametric refinement), not append/dedup/prune over discrete entries. Continual sequential training progressively updates parameters while mitigating catastrophic forgetting.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Yes. Both the WHEN (memory trigger, trained by RL with a reward-adaptive sparsity penalty) and the WHAT (memory weaver, trained by SFT or GRPO toward task reward) are learned policies, not fixed similarity top-k. The trigger is an explicit learned invocation policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent private memory; the weaver/trigger are tied to a specific frozen reasoner. No multi-agent or cross-framework memory sharing is proposed.
benchmarks: ALFWorld, TriviaQA, PopQA, KodCode, BigCodeBench, GPQA, GSM8K, MATH, AQuA; plus out-of-domain generalization tests on ScienceWorld and FEVER. (Abstract cites 'eight benchmarks'; setup text lists nine datasets across five domains.)
benchmark_family: embodied (ALFWorld; out-of-domain ScienceWorld), QA / open-domain (TriviaQA, PopQA; out-of-domain FEVER fact-verification), math (AQuA, GSM8K, MATH), scientific reasoning (GPQA), code (KodCode, BigCodeBench).
baselines: Twelve baselines in four groups: (I) Prompt-based: Vanilla, CoT; (II) Parametric memory: SFT, GRPO, REINFORCE, REINFORCE++, Agent-FLAN; (III) Retrieval-based memory: MemoryBank, ExpeL, Agent Workflow Memory (AWM); (IV) Latent computation: SoftCoT, Co-processor.
key_metrics: Task performance per dataset (accuracy / success rate %), e.g., ALFWorld success rate, QA accuracy, math accuracy, code pass rate. Also relative improvement (%) over baselines, cross-domain transfer accuracy, continual-learning retention, and inference latency (relative to vanilla).
headline_result: Across eight benchmarks MemGen surpasses leading external memory systems (ExpeL, AWM) by up to 38.22% and exceeds GRPO by up to 13.44%. Concrete example: on ALFWorld+SmolLM3-3B, MemGen-GRPO reaches 63.60% (vs vanilla 18.96%, +44.64%); MemGen-SFT 50.60%.
ablations: (1) Latent memory length K sensitivity: performance rises monotonically as K grows 2->32 (more memory capacity). (2) Memory invocation strategy (Table 5): trained Trigger > all-delimiter activation > random insertion (e.g., on GPQA/KodCode/TriviaQA trained trigger 18.28/58.16/65.02 vs all-delimiter 17.34/56.20/64.15 vs random p=0.5 16.66/52.95/57.28), showing selective when/where invocation matters. (3) Weaver parameterization (Table 6): full-parameter SFT > LoRA, but LoRA is competitive and parameter-efficient. (4) Cross-domain generalization (train on one dataset, test on others incl. ScienceWorld/FEVER) and continual learning (Table 4) showing reduced forgetting vs SFT/ExpeL. (5) Post-hoc cluster-removal intervention mapping clusters to planning/procedural/working memory failure modes.
evaluation_decoupling: No. Only end-to-end task metrics are reported; there are no intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k/nDCG) because memory is generated, not retrieved from a labeled corpus. Auxiliary diagnostic analyses (invocation frequency, t-SNE clustering, cluster-removal failure-mode shifts) are reported but are not standard intrinsic retrieval metrics.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Mostly outcome (task accuracy/success). Some process-level analysis is provided: memory invocation frequency across percentile positions, failure-mode breakdown under cluster removal (planning/tool/parsing/formatting errors per Song et al. 2025 taxonomy), and inference latency, giving partial process insight.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Reported as favorable. Despite up to 57.66% performance improvement over vanilla, per-query inference latency stays below the vanilla baseline, ranging from 24% to 94% of vanilla LLM latency (fewer tokens needed to reach correct answers; e.g., MemGen-SFT completes KodCode tasks in 2.94s on Qwen2.5-1.5B). Memory modules are lightweight LoRA adapters (r=16). Trigger sparsity penalty limits unnecessary invocations.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed latent budget per invocation: K latent tokens, K in {2,4,8} in main experiments (ablated 2->32). Number of invocations is adaptive (learned trigger, sentence-granularity, self-scaled to task difficulty). No prompt-token top-k truncation since memory is injected in hidden-state space, not as text.
survey_scope_and_axes: N/A (primary method paper, not a survey).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (uses existing benchmarks via their official training/eval splits; does not construct a new benchmark). Training uses official train splits of all datasets except PopQA, which has no train set and is evaluated with the TriviaQA-trained model to probe cross-dataset generalization.
builds_on: Latent/soft-token reasoning and memory: SoftCoT (Xu et al. 2025), Coconut-style latent reasoning, Co-processor (Liu et al. 2024), LatentSeek, R3Mem (acknowledged in repo). RL fine-tuning: GRPO (DeepSeek), REINFORCE/REINFORCE++. LoRA parameter-efficient adaptation. Search environment from Search-R1. Code framework adapted from LAVIS. Conceptually contrasts with parametric tuning (Agent-FLAN) and retrieval memory (ExpeL, MemoryBank, AWM, G-Memory, AgentKB).
contrasts_with: Parametric memory that modifies reasoner weights (SFT, GRPO, REINFORCE, REINFORCE++, Agent-FLAN); retrieval/text-database memory that externalizes experience (ExpeL, MemoryBank, Agent Workflow Memory/AWM, and by reference G-Memory, AgentKB); other latent-computation methods (SoftCoT, Co-processor). MemGen argues neither parametric nor retrieval memory captures the fluid interweaving of reasoning and memory.
lineage: Group F (decision/experience memory + RL): self-evolving agent memory. Sits in the lineage of experience/case memory for agents (ExpeL, AWM, AgentKB, G-Memory) but pivots from text-retrieval memory to generative latent (machine-native) memory interwoven with reasoning, with RL-learned invocation and weaving policies; bridges latent-reasoning and agent-memory lines.
